items.title: Design system & screens
items.goal: Every MVP screen has an approved pen.dev design built on one set of tokens, and the shared patterns that carry the PRD's rules — AI results labelled as suggestions with their source text, delay status never shown by colour alone, and a typed-name prompt — exist once and are reused everywhere. Designs work at desktop and phone width and read correctly in Simplified Chinese.
prd: UI design → designs in pen.dev, `.pen` files in the repository → decided
UI design → MVP screens table (9 screens) → decided
UI design → design rules 1–5 → suggested
Technical architecture → UI components: Tailwind + shadcn/ui themed from the pen.dev tokens → proposed
Non-functional requirements → Devices: desktop and mobile browsers → decided
exit: `design/tokens.pen` and a readable `design/tokens.md` mirror exist and drive the Tailwind theme
Every MVP screen has a `.pen` frame at desktop and phone width and a `design/specs/<screen>.md` mirror an executor can build from
`AiSuggestion`, `SourceQuote`, `DelayStatusBadge`, `TypedNameDialog` and the empty/loading/error states are built and unit-tested
The accessibility and phone-width standard passes on the shell and the shared patterns
outOfScope: Screen behaviour that needs real data — each feature phase builds its own screen against these designs
A brand identity: there is none yet, so tokens start from a neutral, accessible base
Dark mode beyond mapping the tokens
Client-facing or candidate-facing UI — non-goals for the MVP

items.title: The portal has one visual language defined as tokens
items.story: As a recruiter, I want the portal to look like one product, so that I can read a score, a status and a date the same way on every screen.
ac: Given a designer opens `design/tokens.pen`, when they read it, then colour, type, spacing and radius tokens are all defined with names the Tailwind theme uses.
Given the type stack, when Simplified Chinese text is rendered, then it uses a font that covers the characters (for example Noto Sans SC) and does not fall back to a placeholder glyph.
Given any component, when it is built, then it uses token names and contains no hex colour or raw pixel font size.
prd: UI design → colours, type and spacing defined once as design tokens and mapped to the Tailwind theme → suggested
UI design → design rule 3: the type stack includes a Simplified Chinese font → suggested
Technical architecture → UI components: shadcn/ui themed from the pen.dev tokens → proposed

items.title: Define the colour, type, spacing and radius tokens in pen.dev
items.what: There is no brand yet, so define a neutral, accessible token set from scratch in `design/tokens.pen` through the pen.dev MCP tools, and mirror it to `design/tokens.md` so an executor can build from it without opening pen.dev.
scope: `design/tokens.pen`: colour roles (surface, foreground, muted, primary, destructive, and the delay-status roles), type scale, spacing scale, radii
A type stack including a Simplified Chinese face such as Noto Sans SC
Contrast checked for every text-on-surface pairing at the standard the accessibility record sets
`design/tokens.md` mirror listing every token with its value and its shadcn variable name
exclusions: A brand identity, logo or illustration style
done: `design/tokens.pen` exists and opens in pen.dev with all four token groups
Every text-on-surface pairing meets the contrast rule in `docs/plans/accessibility-standard.md`
`design/tokens.md` lists each token with its value and its target shadcn variable
Delay status has three distinct roles that are distinguishable without colour

items.title: Map the tokens to the Tailwind theme and shadcn CSS variables
items.what: Turn `design/tokens.md` into the app's theme: CSS variables for light and dark, the Tailwind theme configuration for the installed Tailwind major, and the font stack including the Simplified Chinese face.
scope: CSS variables on `:root` and the dark selector, named to match shadcn's conventions
Tailwind theme wired to those variables, following the installed Tailwind major's approach
Font loading for the Latin and Simplified Chinese faces with sensible fallbacks
A lint rule or check that fails on a hex colour or raw pixel font size in `src/components`
exclusions: Changing token values — the design file is the source
Dark-mode design work beyond mapping the tokens
done: Every token in `design/tokens.md` has a CSS variable and a Tailwind token with the same name
A page renders Simplified Chinese text in the intended font with no fallback boxes
The guard fails a deliberate hex colour added to a component

items.title: Recruiters can navigate the portal on desktop and on a phone
items.story: As a recruiter, I want to move between the dashboard, jobs, search, placements and settings on whatever device I have, so that I can work from my desk or from a client's lobby.
ac: Given the app shell on desktop, when I look at the navigation, then every MVP area is reachable in one click.
Given the app shell at 390 px, when I open any page, then navigation is usable, nothing is cut off and the page does not scroll horizontally.
Given keyboard-only use, when I tab through the shell, then focus is visible and every navigation target is reachable.
prd: UI design → MVP screens table → decided
UI design → design rule 4: the dashboard and pipeline board are fully usable at phone width → suggested
Non-functional requirements → Devices: desktop and mobile browsers → decided

items.title: Design the app shell and navigation at desktop and phone width
items.what: Design the frame every screen sits in: navigation, page header, content area and the recruiter-name affordance, at both desktop and phone width, following the navigation map from Phase 0.
scope: `design/shell.pen` with desktop (1440) and phone (390) frames
Navigation for the nine MVP areas, collapsing sensibly on a phone
Where the typed recruiter name is shown and changed
`design/specs/shell.md` mirror: structure, spacing, states and phone behaviour
done: Both frames exist in `design/shell.pen` and cover every MVP area
`design/specs/shell.md` describes the phone collapse behaviour precisely enough to build from
The name affordance appears in both frames

items.title: Build the app shell layout and navigation
items.what: Build the shell from `design/specs/shell.md` as a Server Component layout with a small client island for the mobile navigation, using shadcn/ui primitives and the theme tokens only.
scope: `src/app/layout.tsx` and `src/components/patterns/AppShell.tsx`
Navigation links for the nine MVP areas, with routes that may still be placeholders
Mobile navigation in a sheet; desktop navigation persistent
Playwright coverage at both widths: navigation works, focus is visible, no horizontal overflow at 390 px
done: The shell matches `design/specs/shell.md` at both widths on review
Playwright passes at `desktop` and `phone`, including the no-horizontal-overflow assertion
Keyboard navigation reaches every link with visible focus

items.title: Shared patterns make AI results and delays unambiguous
items.story: As a recruiter, I want every AI result to say it is a suggestion and show me the text it came from, and every delay status to be readable without relying on colour, so that I can trust what I act on.
ac: Given any AI-derived value on screen, when it is displayed, then it carries a visible 'AI suggestion' label, and a score also shows its model version and date.
Given an AI-derived value, when I expand its source, then the exact CV or job text it came from is shown, marked `lang="zh-Hans"` when it is Chinese.
Given a delay status, when it is displayed, then it shows an icon or word as well as colour and carries an `aria-label` stating the status in full.
Given my first change on this device, when I act, then the portal asks for my name and remembers it on that device.
prd: AI governance → requirement 1: every score, flag and parsed field shows the text it was based on → proposed
AI governance → requirement 2: each AI output is stored with its input, model version and date → proposed
UI design → design rule 1: every AI result is labelled as a suggestion → suggested
UI design → design rule 2: delay status uses a word or icon as well as colour → suggested
UI design → design rule 5: the portal asks for the recruiter's name before their first change on a device → suggested

items.title: Design the shared patterns: AI suggestion, source quote, delay badge, name prompt and states
items.what: Design the five patterns that carry the PRD's rules, so every screen inherits them instead of reinventing them: the AI-suggestion label with model version and date, the expandable source quote, the delay-status badge, the typed-name prompt, and the empty, loading and error states.
scope: `design/patterns.pen` with a frame per pattern at desktop and phone width
Delay badge: three statuses, each with icon, word and colour, plus the end-state and Placed cases that have no status
Source quote: collapsed and expanded, English and Simplified Chinese
Typed-name prompt: first use, remembered name, and changing the name
`design/specs/patterns.md` mirror with the props each pattern needs
exclusions: Copywriting beyond the label text the PRD requires
done: All five patterns exist as frames at both widths
The delay badge is legible in greyscale, proving it does not depend on colour
The Chinese source-quote frame uses the Simplified Chinese face and truncates without cutting characters
`design/specs/patterns.md` lists each pattern's props and states
verify: greyscale check of the delay badge frame

items.title: Build AiSuggestion, SourceQuote, DelayStatusBadge, TypedNameDialog and the state components
items.what: Build the five shared patterns from `design/specs/patterns.md` with unit tests. Their logic — badge wording and aria text, name validation and device persistence — is test-first.
scope: `src/components/patterns/`: `AiSuggestion`, `SourceQuote`, `DelayStatusBadge`, `TypedNameDialog`, `EmptyState`, `ErrorState` and loading skeletons

Failing tests first: badge text and `aria-label` per status; end states and Placed render no status; name validation rejects blank and whitespace; the remembered name persists on the device and can be changed
`SourceQuote` sets `lang="zh-Hans"` for Chinese text and truncates with CSS, never by slicing strings
`AiSuggestion` requires a model version and date when the value is a score
exclusions: Wiring the patterns into any screen
Server-side persistence of the recruiter name — it is remembered on the device
done: Failing-then-passing unit tests cover badge wording and aria text, end-state handling, name validation and device persistence
`SourceQuote` renders Chinese text with `lang="zh-Hans"` and CSS truncation, proven by a test with a long Chinese string
`AiSuggestion` fails typecheck when a score is passed without a model version and date
Each component matches its frame in `design/specs/patterns.md` on review

items.title: Every MVP screen has an approved design
items.story: As a recruiter, I want each screen designed before it is built, so that what I get matches how I actually work rather than how the data happens to be shaped.
ac: Given the PRD screen list, when each screen is designed, then it has desktop and phone frames in `design/` and a `design/specs/<screen>.md` mirror.
Given a screen shows AI output or delay status, when it is designed, then it uses the shared patterns rather than a one-off treatment.
Given the dashboard and the pipeline board, when they are designed at 390 px, then every action on them is reachable without horizontal page scrolling.
prd: UI design → MVP screens table: Dashboard, Jobs, Job detail, Job form, Candidate search, Candidate profile, Pipeline board, Placements, Settings → decided
UI design → design rules 1–5 → suggested
CV processing → requirement 2: a review queue for files that fail to parse → proposed (screen not in the PRD list)

items.title: Design the Dashboard
items.what: Design the screen recruiters open first: overdue candidates ordered by days over, due-soon candidates, guarantee end dates, and filters for client, job, stage and owner. It must be fully usable at phone width.
scope: `design/screens/dashboard.pen` with desktop and phone frames
Overdue list ordered by days over, with the delay badge pattern and a 'waiting on' column
Due-soon section and guarantee-ending section
Filters: client, job, stage, owner — in a sheet at phone width
Empty, loading and error states
`design/specs/dashboard.md` mirror
exclusions: Any email or push alert — the portal sends none
Charts or metrics dashboards: the four success metrics belong to the real-data release
done: Both frames exist and use the shared delay badge and state patterns
Every filter in the PRD appears and is reachable at 390 px
`design/specs/dashboard.md` states the sort order and what each section shows when empty
verify: phone frame has no horizontal overflow

items.title: Design the Jobs list and Job detail screens
items.what: Design how recruiters browse jobs and work one job: the list with status, owner, open gap flags and candidates per stage; the detail with requirements, the gap-flag checklist, ranked matches with scores and reasons, and the pipeline board.
scope: `design/screens/jobs.pen`: list and detail, desktop and phone frames
List: status, owner, open gap-flag count, candidates per stage
Detail: requirements, gap-flag checklist with the client question, ranked matches using the AI-suggestion and source-quote patterns, embedded pipeline board
The open-flag banner with its count
`design/specs/jobs.md` and `design/specs/job-detail.md` mirrors
done: List and detail frames exist at both widths
Ranked matches show score, reasons and source text through the shared patterns, with the model version and date
The open-flag banner appears and states that matching is not blocked
verify: both widths present for both screens

items.title: Design the Job form including JD upload and the requirement reason field
items.what: Design the form recruiters use to create or edit a job: must-have and nice-to-have requirements, job-description upload that pre-fills the same form, and the reason field that must be written before nationality or language can count.
scope: `design/screens/job-form.pen`, desktop and phone frames
Requirement rows with a must-have / nice-to-have choice
JD upload and the confirm-the-pre-filled-values state
Nationality and language marked as required only alongside a written reason, with the reason field blocking until filled
Validation and error states
`design/specs/job-form.md` mirror
exclusions: The gap-check result display (that is on Job detail, T02)
done: The must-have / nice-to-have choice appears on every requirement row
The nationality and language reason field is visibly required before either can count, per the PRD decision
The JD-upload pre-fill state shows the recruiter what was read and asks them to confirm
verify: reason-field requirement visible in the frame

items.title: Design the Candidate search and Candidate profile screens
items.what: Design how recruiters find people and check one person: a plain-language search box with filters and CV dates, and a profile showing parsed fields with their source text, edit mode, the original file and stage history.
scope: `design/screens/search.pen`: search box, filters (skills, years, location, language, CV date), results with last-updated date
`design/screens/candidate.pen`: parsed fields with source quotes, edit mode, link to the original file, stage history
How a recruiter-edited field is shown as differing from the parsed value
Empty, loading and error states for both
`design/specs/search.md` and `design/specs/candidate.md` mirrors
exclusions: External talent sources — a non-goal, though the filter area should not preclude a future source switch
done: All five PRD filters appear and collapse into a sheet at phone width
Every parsed field on the profile can show the CV text it came from
An edited field is visually distinguishable from a parsed one, and edit mode shows the typed-name prompt

items.title: Design the Pipeline board, phone width first
items.what: Design the board recruiters use to move candidates: one column per stage, the delay status shown with a word or icon as well as colour, and a typed-name prompt on every move. The PRD requires it to be fully usable at phone width, so design that width first.
scope: `design/screens/pipeline.pen`: phone frame first, then desktop
Seven stages plus the three end states, with Placed and end states showing no delay status
Moving a candidate without drag: a menu or button that works by keyboard
The typed-name prompt on each move
`design/specs/pipeline.md` mirror including the phone column behaviour
exclusions: Any AI-initiated move — the AI never advances a candidate
done: The phone frame is designed first and every action on it is reachable without horizontal page scrolling
End states and Placed show no delay status, matching the pipeline rules
A non-drag move path is designed and reachable by keyboard
verify: phone frame designed and free of horizontal overflow

items.title: Design the Placements and Settings screens
items.what: Design the post-placement follow-up and the rules screen: start-date confirmation with the 30-day guarantee countdown, and stage limits at default, client and job level with the public-holiday list and the change log.
scope: `design/screens/placements.pen`: start-date check, guarantee countdown, the 5-working-day flag
`design/screens/settings.pen`: stage limits at three levels, public holidays, change log
How the limit hierarchy (job over client over default) is made visible
`design/specs/placements.md` and `design/specs/settings.md` mirrors
exclusions: Retention settings — those belong to the real-data release
User or role management — there is no sign-in
done: The guarantee countdown and the 5-working-day flag both appear
The limit hierarchy is legible: a recruiter can see which level a limit came from
The change log shows the typed name and the date for each entry
verify: limit hierarchy visible in the settings frame

items.title: Design the CV review queue screen
items.what: The PRD requires a review queue for files that fail to parse, but the screen is not in its screen list. Confirm the screen with the product owner, then design it: the failed files, the reason each failed, and a retry action.
scope: Confirmation with the product owner that this screen is in the MVP, recorded in the open-questions register
`design/screens/review-queue.pen` at desktop and phone width
Per file: name, reason (including the scanned-file rejection message), and retry
`design/specs/review-queue.md` mirror
exclusions: OCR or any attempt to read scanned files — an explicit non-goal
Uploading files — the MVP loads samples through the seed
done: The product owner's answer is recorded in `docs/decisions/open-questions.md` before the design is finalised
Both frames exist and show the rejection reason in recruiter language
The retry action is clearly a recruiter action, not an automatic one
verify: open-questions register updated with the answer

items.title: Screens meet the accessibility and phone-width standard automatically
items.story: As a recruiter using a phone in a client's lobby, or a keyboard because my mouse has died, I want every screen to stay usable, so that the portal does not become the reason I cannot do my job.
ac: Given any key screen, when the end-to-end suite runs at 390 px, then the page does not scroll horizontally.
Given any key screen, when the accessibility scan runs, then it reports no violation at the level the standard sets.
Given a new screen is added without meeting the standard, when CI runs, then the check fails rather than passing silently.
prd: UI design → design rule 2: status uses a word or icon as well as colour → suggested
UI design → design rule 4: the dashboard and pipeline board are fully usable at phone width → suggested
Non-functional requirements → Devices: desktop and mobile browsers → decided

items.title: Add the shared phone-width and status-legibility assertions
items.what: Add reusable Playwright helpers every screen test can call: no horizontal overflow at phone width, and every delay status carries a word or icon plus an `aria-label`. Then apply them to the shell.
scope: `e2e/helpers/a11y.ts`: `expectNoHorizontalOverflow(page)` and `expectStatusNotColourOnly(page)`
Applied to the shell test as the first user
Documentation in the test strategy record so every screen task uses them
exclusions: Fixing violations on screens that do not exist yet
done: Both helpers exist and are used by at least one passing test
A deliberately overflowing element makes the overflow assertion fail
A status rendered with colour only makes the second assertion fail

items.title: Add the axe accessibility scan to the end-to-end suite
items.what: Add an automated accessibility scan to the Playwright suite at the level the accessibility standard sets, wired so each screen task can add its page in one line, and fix anything it finds on the shell and the shared patterns.
scope: The axe Playwright integration as a dev dependency (the accessibility standard authorises it)
A shared `expectNoA11yViolations(page)` helper with the agreed rule set and any documented exceptions
Applied to the shell and a patterns gallery page
Any violation found on the shell or patterns fixed in this task
exclusions: Screens that do not exist yet
Changing token values — raise a finding if contrast fails
done: The scan runs in the end-to-end suite and passes on the shell and the shared patterns
A deliberately unlabelled input makes the scan fail
Any exception to the rule set is written down with its reason
